title: A Text That Evolves

spine.markdown:
Intertext thus offers two features that distinguish it from most existing systems:

- With the exception of opening section vignettes, there is no canonical text. Instead, the text takes shape in interaction with the reader.
- With the reader’s permission, the system evaluates and absorbs their material into the spine or fund.

The text thus evolves with each reader and each reading. The goal is to facilitate a collaborative text that nevertheless maintains a degree of authorial guidance and control (Compare the interactive narrative authoring system Drama Llama, Sun et al. 2025)

fundEntries.title: The proposal
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks what happens to a conversation after a contributing reader finishes.
fundEntries.markdown: When a contributing reader finishes a section, a first pass of the model compares the conversation with the current spine and fund. It may propose no change at all, a revision of passages in the spine, new units for the fund, revisions or replacements of existing units, or sources to support them. Corrections and changes in proportion to the main movement of the section belong in the spine; optional material belongs in the fund.

fundEntries.title: The review and the checks
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks who or what decides whether a contribution changes the text, or how bad contributions are kept out.
fundEntries.markdown: A separate pass then reviews each proposed change for its fidelity to the work, its relevance, duplication, the quality of its prose and rhythm, its proportion, and its need for sources, and checks that a unit is attached at a point where what it presupposes has already been introduced. The review may accept an addition, hold it as a candidate that readers do not see, or reject it, and it may not accept material whose facts still need to be verified. A further set of checks rejects invented sources and excessive growth. If nothing survives, the section remains as it was.

fundEntries.title: Candidate, accepted, superseded, rejected
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks what happens to material that is not accepted, or whether anything is ever deleted.
fundEntries.markdown: Every unit of the fund has a status. A candidate is under evaluation and is never offered to readers; an accepted unit is available to the text; a superseded unit has been replaced by another; a rejected unit is kept as a record of the decision. Nothing is deleted. Each unit also records whether it needs sources and has them, and where it came from: the author's text, a reader's conversation, the author's own editing, or a proposal by the model.

fundEntries.title: Versions
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks how versions are kept, or whether a change can affect a reading in progress.
fundEntries.markdown: Approved changes become a new version of the section, stored complete and never altered afterwards. A version replaces the current one only if that version is still current, so two contributions arriving together cannot overwrite each other. A reader already in a section stays with the version in which the reading began, and the next reader receives the new one. Versions can be exported, so that the record of the text does not depend on the database that serves it.

fundEntries.title: What the author controls
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks how the author keeps control of a text that readers change, or who is the author of an evolved text.
fundEntries.markdown: Routine editorial decisions are left to the model, but the rules are the author's. The author writes or approves the statements of each section's argument, the opening vignettes and the lists of references and media, and sets the policy that the editorial passes follow. A separate editor allows the author to read every section, revise the prose of the spine and any unit of the fund, add units, change their status, and publish the result as a new version. Every unit keeps a record of its origin, so the mixture of hands in an evolved text is preserved.

fundEntries.title: What the editorial tools cannot yet do
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks about the limits of the current system or what an author cannot yet do.
fundEntries.markdown: The author's editor currently runs only on the author's own machine, and there is not yet a secure version online. It cannot compare or restore versions or show the full history of changes, although a version can be exported. Units of the fund may be grouped into a named sequence, but the text does not yet offer such a sequence to the reader as a path through the material.
